messages.author: b0f830cb2187ba6f
messages.subject: Shiny server restricted access?
parts:
Hello,

In one day and a half, I just discovered Shiny and Shiny server, created my first local application, then installed an online shiny server, and everything is great! BTW thanks for these packages.

Now I'd like to secure my online application. How to do that?

I do not want to restrict the access to the whole /var/shiny-server/www/ directory, rather to /var/shiny-server/www/myPrivateApp/

I tried setting .htaccess and .htpasswd files in my app's directory, but I guess the standard apache setting is of no use here? Or is it?

Has anyone a clue about how to do that?

Best regards

Thibault

messages.author: a577395f57165d80
messages.subject: Re: Shiny server restricted access?
parts:
No I didn't succeed that way.

Finally, I think the best way in the long run is to play with session variables. Which I didn't tried out yet.

For the moment I opted for a temporary solution: a text field and two buttons: "lock" and "unlock". A passphrase is defined on the server side. This key must be entered in the text field and "unlock" sends the value to the server. If the key is correct, all the rest of the application is made visible to the user.

Now the trick is that, if you define the rest of the application -which is supposed to be protected- on the client side within a simple conditionalPanel(), your protection will be very poor: the supposedly protected content is merely "hidden" by javascript/css, but still accessible from the source code of the page. So you have to define all the protected content on the server side, and use a renderUI() on server side, coupled with a uiOutput() on client side.

Finally, almost everything is defined on server side, and almost nothing on the client side, except for the lock/unlock panel.

I believe that using the combination .htaccess and .htpasswd files should be working (I did not try it myself). 
I succeeded in a similar way using nginx instead of Apache to get things lighter and using the htpasswd files. The customer accesses its own area with login and password and then can browse through its own shiny apps. 
I also added an SSL layer (HTTPS) to make things secured. Let me know if you need more details (I guess it would be too long to explain it on a forum). 

JB
